# Medical Wound Healing Accelerator and Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

## Wound Healing Accelerator

The medical wound healing accelerator is designed to promote and expedite the healing process at wound sites associated with external fracture fixation. The device features a body that attaches detachably to the fixing pin of an external fracture fixator, which is inserted through the skin into the bone. This detachable design allows for convenient installation and removal, providing flexibility during patient treatment and care.

On one side of the body, the device incorporates multiple light source units. These units emit beneficial healing light directly onto the skin in the area surrounding the wound. By delivering therapeutic light to the affected region, the device aims to stimulate tissue repair and accelerate the natural healing process at the pin insertion site.

To ensure precise and effective operation, a controller is electrically connected to the light source units. This controller manages and regulates the functioning of the light sources, allowing for controlled delivery of the therapeutic light according to the treatment requirements.

## Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

A related device is provided for the treatment of osteomyelitis, a condition characterized by bone infection. This treatment device utilizes an insert that can be placed directly into an infected bone region. The insert is equipped with several light-emitting members positioned in a spaced-apart arrangement along its length, enabling the delivery of therapeutic light throughout the affected area.

A key feature of the insert is its adaptability. It can be cut or bent at the gaps between the individual light-emitting members, allowing it to be customized to match the specific shape and contours of the osteomyelitis-affected area. This adjustable design ensures that the treatment can be tailored to the unique anatomy and requirements of each patient, providing targeted therapy precisely where it is needed.

# Medical Wound Healing Accelerator and Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to medical devices that utilize light therapy to promote healing and treat infection. More specifically, it concerns a wound healing accelerator designed for use in conjunction with external fixators, as well as a specialized device for the treatment of osteomyelitis, a bacterial or fungal infection of bone tissue.

## Background

Patients undergoing orthopedic treatment frequently require external fixators, which are stabilizing devices attached to bone through fixing pins that pass through the skin. These pin sites are prone to complications, including delayed wound healing and infection, because the skin is continuously penetrated by the fixation hardware. Conventional wound care at these sites often relies on topical treatments and manual dressing changes, which can be inconsistent and slow to produce results.

Similarly, osteomyelitis—an infection of the bone—presents significant treatment challenges. The affected regions are often irregularly shaped and difficult to access, making it hard to deliver therapeutic agents precisely where they are needed. There is therefore a need for devices capable of delivering targeted, controlled therapy to both surface wounds and deep bone infections.

## Summary of the Invention

### Wound Healing Accelerator

The first aspect of the invention discloses a medical wound healing accelerator. This device comprises a body that is detachably mounted onto the fixing pin of an external fixator. Because the body can be attached and removed as needed, it can be conveniently applied during treatment and taken off for cleaning, adjustment, or replacement without disturbing the underlying fixation system.

The body is equipped with multiple light source units. These units are arranged to emit beneficial therapeutic light directly onto the skin surrounding the pin site. By exposing the wound area to specific wavelengths of light known to stimulate cellular activity, reduce inflammation, and promote tissue regeneration, the device accelerates the natural healing process at the vulnerable point where the pin enters the body.

The operation of the light source units is governed by a controller that is electrically connected to the body. The controller allows the intensity, duration, and timing of the light emission to be regulated, ensuring that the therapy is delivered safely and effectively according to the patient's needs and the treatment protocol.

### Osteomyelitis Treatment Device

The second aspect of the invention presents a device specifically designed for the treatment of osteomyelitis. This device features an insertable component that can be introduced into or positioned adjacent to the infected bone region. Along the length of this component, a series of light-emitting members are arranged at spaced intervals, allowing therapeutic light to be delivered across an extended area rather than at a single point.

A key feature of this device is the adaptability of the insertable component. It is constructed so that it can be cut or bent to conform to the specific shape, size, and contour of the affected area. This flexibility ensures that the light-emitting members can be positioned to closely follow the geometry of the infection site, enabling precise, targeted light therapy even in irregular or hard-to-reach regions of bone.

By directing therapeutic light onto the infected tissue, the device supports the treatment of bone infection, potentially reducing bacterial activity, stimulating healing, and complementing other therapeutic measures.

## Advantages

Together, these devices provide effective, targeted, and controllable light-based therapy for two distinct but related clinical challenges. The wound healing accelerator improves outcomes at external fixator pin sites through convenient, detachable application and controlled light delivery, while the osteomyelitis treatment device offers a customizable, shape-conforming means of treating bone infections with precision. Both devices harness the therapeutic benefits of light to enhance patient recovery and reduce complications.

# Patent Abstract

**PHOTOTHERAPEUTIC DEVICE AND METHOD FOR ENHANCING PIN-SITE WOUND HEALING AND TREATING OSTEOMYELITIS IN EXTERNAL FIXATION**

## Abstract

A phototherapeutic medical device and associated method are disclosed for accelerating wound healing at external fixator pin sites and for treating osteomyelitis. The device comprises a plurality of light-emitting elements configured to deliver therapeutic electromagnetic radiation at wavelengths within the red and near-infrared spectrum (approximately 630 nm to 940 nm) to tissue surrounding percutaneous fixation pins. In certain embodiments, the device includes an annular or modular housing that removably couples to one or more fixator pins, positioning the light-emitting elements in circumferential alignment with the pin-tissue interface to provide substantially uniform irradiation of the peri-pin wound margin.

The device further incorporates a controller programmed to regulate irradiance, wavelength selection, pulse frequency, and treatment duration according to predetermined therapeutic protocols. Selected wavelengths and dosimetry parameters are configured to stimulate cellular photobiomodulation, thereby promoting angiogenesis, reducing local inflammation, enhancing fibroblast and osteoblast activity, and exhibiting antimicrobial effects against pathogens associated with pin-site infection and osteomyelitis, including biofilm-forming bacteria.

In additional embodiments, the device includes one or more sensors for monitoring tissue temperature, wound condition, or infection markers, enabling adaptive adjustment of treatment parameters. A power source, which may be portable or rechargeable, permits ambulatory use, allowing continuous or intermittent therapy without immobilizing the patient. The device may optionally combine phototherapy with adjunctive antimicrobial agents delivered to the pin site.

The disclosed device and method reduce the incidence of pin-site infection, shorten wound-healing time, and provide a noninvasive therapeutic modality for managing superficial and deep osseous infection in patients undergoing external fixation.

---

# Abstract

A phototherapeutic system for accelerating wound healing and treating bone infection is disclosed. In one aspect, the system comprises a wound healing accelerator configured to attach to one or more fracture fixation pins extending percutaneously through tissue. The accelerator includes one or more light source units mountable to the fixation pins, positioned to direct therapeutic light toward the pin-tissue interface and surrounding wound site. By coupling to existing external fixation hardware, the light source units deliver targeted phototherapy to the periwound region, promoting cellular activity, reducing pin-site infection risk, and accelerating soft tissue and bone healing without requiring additional invasive fixation.

In another aspect, an insertable device is provided for the treatment of osteomyelitis. The device comprises an elongate body dimensioned for insertion into an intramedullary canal or bone cavity and carries a plurality of spaced light-emitting members distributed along its length. The spaced arrangement of the light-emitting members provides substantially uniform illumination of the infected bone and adjacent tissue, delivering antimicrobial and healing-promoting light along an extended treatment region. The light-emitting members may be independently controllable to tailor light dosage, wavelength, and treatment duration to the infection site.

The disclosed system enables localized, hardware-integrated, and minimally invasive delivery of therapeutic light for enhanced wound healing and effective management of bone infections, including chronic and post-surgical osteomyelitis.

# Patent Abstract

## Phototherapeutic Apparatus and Method for Treatment of External Fixator Pin Site Infections and Osteomyelitis

**Abstract**

A phototherapeutic apparatus and associated method are disclosed for the localized treatment of pin site wounds associated with external fixation devices and for the management of osteomyelitis in underlying bone tissue. The invention comprises an annular light-delivery collar configured to be releasably mounted circumferentially about a percutaneous fixator pin or wire at the skin interface. The collar houses a plurality of radially distributed light-emitting diodes (LEDs) arranged to emit electromagnetic radiation in at least two discrete wavelength bands: a first band in the antimicrobial blue spectrum (approximately 400–470 nm) directed toward the superficial pin site wound to reduce bacterial colonization, and a second band in the near-infrared spectrum (approximately 800–900 nm) configured for deeper tissue penetration to stimulate cellular photobiomodulation within cortical and medullary bone affected by osteomyelitis.

In a preferred embodiment, the apparatus further comprises an elongate intramedullary or peri-cortical optical waveguide couplable to the fixator pin, whereby near-infrared radiation is conducted along the pin shaft to deliver therapeutic light directly to infected osseous tissue at depth. The waveguide includes a light-diffusing distal segment having circumferential emission characteristics to provide substantially uniform irradiation of the surrounding bone.

The device includes an onboard microcontroller, a rechargeable power source, and a programmable dosimetry module configured to regulate irradiance, wavelength selection, pulse frequency, and treatment duration according to predetermined therapeutic protocols. An integrated sensor array, comprising temperature and optical feedback elements, monitors tissue response and provides closed-loop control to prevent thermal injury while maintaining therapeutic fluence within a target range of approximately 4–60 J/cm².

The method comprises positioning the annular collar about the pin site, selectively activating the blue-spectrum emitters for antimicrobial surface decontamination and the near-infrared emitters for deep photobiomodulation of infected bone, and adjusting delivered dose based on sensor feedback. The invention thereby provides concurrent, non-invasive management of superficial pin site infection and deep osteomyelitis without removal of the external fixation hardware, reducing antibiotic dependency and improving osseointegration at the pin-bone interface.

---
